The Benue State Police Command has rescued eight kidnap victims, including the Catholic priest of Otukpo Diocese, Rev. Fr. John Otache. The Command’s spokesperson, Peter Aondongu, stated this in a release issued on Monday and made available to journalists in Makurdi, the state capital. According to the statement, two suspects were arrested during the rescue operation. Aondongu explained that the Catholic priest and the seven victims were kidnapped last Tuesday while returning from a village market along the Ugbokolo–Ajegbe–Awume Road, before Ipiga Village in the Ohimini Local Government Area of the state. The statement read in part, “Upon receipt of the report, operatives of the Command, in conjunction with personnel of the Police Mobile Force and the Benue State Civil Protection Guards, were immediately mobilised to the area and launched a coordinated rescue operation. He said that the State Commissioner of Police, Cletus Nwadiogbu, appreciated the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu and the Assistant IG, Police Mobile Force, for their support to the Command in the ongoing fight against violent crime in the state. He noted that the CP also commended the operatives for their prompt response, professionalism and commitment to the protection of lives and property. The command, however, reassured residents of the state of its readiness and determination to sustain intelligence-led operations and deny criminal elements the opportunity to threaten the peace and security of the state. The command also called on members of the public to continue to support the police with timely and credible information that could assist ongoing operations. John Charles
